Anatomy 05.question: ১) Which is not a salivary gland?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The parathyroid gland is an endocrine gland located behind the thyroid gland; it is not a salivary gland.

The three major paired salivary glands are:

  • Parotid

  • Submandibular

  • Sublingual

Exam pearl:
“Major salivary glands = Parotid + Submandibular + Sublingual.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২) What is structural & functional unit of kidney?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney. Each kidney contains approximately 1 million nephrons.

A nephron consists mainly of:

  • Renal corpuscle → glomerulus + Bowman's capsule

  • Renal tubule → PCT + loop of Henle + DCT

Exam pearl:
“Structural & functional unit of kidney = Nephron.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩) Serous demilune is characteristic of which gland?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Serous demilunes (Gianuzzi's demilunes) are classically seen in mixed salivary glands, especially the submandibular gland.

  • Submandibular → mixed gland, predominantly serous + serous demilunes

  • Sublingual → mixed gland, predominantly mucous + serous demilunes

  • Parotid → purely serous

  • Parathyroid → endocrine gland

Exam pearl:
“Serous demilunes → mixed salivary glands; classically submandibular.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪) What is the length of male urethra?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Explanation:
The male urethra is approximately 18–20 cm long in an adult male.

It has four parts:

  • Preprostatic

  • Prostatic

  • Membranous

  • Spongy (penile)

Female urethra is much shorter, approximately 4 cm long.

Exam pearl:
“Male urethra ≈ 20 cm; female urethra ≈ 4 cm.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৫) Which one is outer most covering of testis?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The tunica vaginalis is the outermost serous covering of the testis. It is derived from the processus vaginalis of the peritoneum.

From outside inward, the important coverings include:
Tunica vaginalis → tunica albuginea → tunica vasculosa

  • Tunica vaginalis → outermost serous covering

  • Tunica albuginea → tough fibrous capsule

  • Tunica vasculosa → vascular layer deep to tunica albuginea

Exam pearl:
“Outer covering of testis = Tunica vaginalis.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৬) Centroacinar cells are unique to.........?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Centroacinar cells are a distinctive histological feature of the exocrine pancreas. They represent the beginning of the intercalated ducts and are located within the center of pancreatic acini.

  • Pancreas → centroacinar cells present

  • Parotid → absent

  • Submandibular → absent

  • Sublingual → absent

Exam pearl:
“Centroacinar cells = Pancreas.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৭) What type of muscles are present in tongue?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The muscles of the tongue are skeletal (striated) muscles. They are divided into:

  • Intrinsic muscles → change the shape of the tongue

  • Extrinsic muscles → change the position of the tongue

Both types are composed of skeletal muscle and are under voluntary control.

Exam pearl:
“Tongue muscles = skeletal muscle.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৮) Which is not a feature of proximal convoluted tubule (PCT)?
Anatomy 05.option2: simple cuboidal cells with long microvilli
Anatomy 05.exp:
The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) is highly active in reabsorption, so its cells require a large amount of ATP and therefore contain numerous mitochondria, not few.

Features of PCT:

  • Mainly located in the renal cortex

  • Simple cuboidal epithelium with prominent long microvilli (brush border)

  • Numerous mitochondria → support active transport

  • Interdigitating basolateral folds → increase surface area for transport

Exam pearl:
“PCT = brush border + numerous mitochondria + basolateral infoldings.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৯) Which produces the false capsule of kidney?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The renal fascia (Gerota’s fascia) forms the false capsule around the kidney by enclosing the kidney and surrounding perinephric fat.

Kidney coverings from inside → outside:

  1. Fibrous (true) capsule

  2. Perinephric fat

  3. Renal fascia (false capsule)

  4. Paranephric fat

Exam pearl:
“True capsule = Fibrous capsule; False capsule = Renal fascia.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১০) The visceral layer of a renal corpuscle consists of unusual stellate epithelial cells are called......
Anatomy 05.exp:
The visceral layer of Bowman's capsule consists of specialized, highly branched epithelial cells called podocytes.

Podocytes have foot processes (pedicels) that interdigitate around the glomerular capillaries and form filtration slits, which are essential components of the glomerular filtration barrier.

  • Podocytes → visceral layer of Bowman's capsule

  • Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells → modified smooth muscle cells of afferent arteriole

  • Mesangial cells → support and regulate glomerular capillaries

  • Brush border → microvilli, prominent in PCT

Exam pearl:
“Visceral layer of renal corpuscle = Podocytes.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১১) Which is the largest internal organ of the body?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The liver is the largest internal organ of the human body, weighing approximately 1.2–1.5 kg in an adult.

  • Liver → largest internal organ

  • Skin → largest organ overall

  • Brain → much smaller than liver

  • Intestine → long but not the largest internal organ by mass

Exam pearl:
“Largest organ = Skin; Largest internal organ = Liver.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১২) Which cell is a modified smooth muscle cell that secretes renin?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells are modified smooth muscle cells located mainly in the wall of the afferent arteriole. They synthesize and secrete renin.

  • JG cells → secrete renin

  • Macula densa → senses tubular NaCl concentration

  • Mesangial cells → structural/supportive and contractile functions

  • Podocytes → form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule

Exam pearl:
“Modified smooth muscle cell + renin = Juxtaglomerular cell.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৩) Interstitial cells of leydig secrete-
Anatomy 05.exp:
Leydig (interstitial) cells are located between the seminiferous tubules of the testes and secrete testosterone in response to LH.

  • Leydig cells → Testosterone

  • Sertoli cells → Inhibin B + Androgen-binding protein (ABP) + Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH)

Exam pearl:
“LH → Leydig cells → Testosterone.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৪) What is space of Disse?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The Space of Disse is the perisinusoidal space located between the sinusoidal endothelial cells and hepatocytes in the liver.

It contains:

  • Hepatocyte microvilli

  • Hepatic stellate (Ito) cells

  • Extracellular matrix

It is an important site for exchange of nutrients, metabolites, and plasma components between the blood and hepatocytes.

Exam pearl:
“Space of Disse = Perisinusoidal space.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৫) Which is true about ileum?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The ileum has a continuous mesenteric border without a “window” because the arterial arcades are more numerous and the mesenteric vessels extend closer to the intestinal wall.

Key features of ileum:

  • Peyer’s patches → numerous

  • Solitary lymphoid follicles → numerous

  • Villi → short and finger-like, not leaf-like

  • Mesenteric window → absent

Exam pearl:
“Ileum → numerous Peyer’s patches + no window in mesentery.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৬) Which one is not covering of spermatic cord?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The dartos muscle is a layer of the scrotal wall, not a covering of the spermatic cord.

The spermatic cord coverings are derived from the abdominal wall:

  • External spermatic fascia → external oblique aponeurosis

  • Cremasteric muscle/fascia → internal oblique

  • Internal spermatic fascia → transversalis fascia

Exam pearl:
“Spermatic cord coverings = External spermatic fascia + Cremasteric fascia/muscle + Internal spermatic fascia.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৭) Which description is true of the gallbladder?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The gallbladder does not produce bile. It stores and concentrates bile by absorbing water and electrolytes from it.

  • Liver → produces/secretes bile

  • Gallbladder → stores and concentrates bile

  • Gallbladder contraction → releases bile into the duodenum

Exam pearl:
“Liver makes bile; gallbladder stores and concentrates bile.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৮) What type of epithelium lines the prostatic urethra?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The prostatic urethra is lined mainly by transitional epithelium (urothelium), which is continuous with the epithelium of the urinary bladder.

  • Prostatic urethra → Transitional epithelium

  • Membranous urethra → Pseudostratified/stratified columnar

  • Most of penile urethra → Pseudostratified columnar

  • External urethral meatus → Stratified squamous

Exam pearl:
“Prostatic urethra = Transitional epithelium.”

Anatomy 05.question: ১৯) Which one is internal genital organ?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The vagina is an internal female genital organ.

  • Vagina → internal genital organ

  • Labia minora → external genitalia (vulva)

  • Vestibule → part of the vulva

  • Clitoris → external genitalia

Exam pearl:
“Internal female genital organs → Vagina + uterus + uterine tubes + ovaries.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২০) Which structure rest on superior pole of each kidney?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The adrenal (suprarenal) gland lies on the superior pole of each kidney.

  • Right adrenal gland → pyramidal

  • Left adrenal gland → crescent/semi-lunar

  • Both are retroperitoneal endocrine glands.

Exam pearl:
“Superior pole of kidney → Adrenal (suprarenal) gland.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২১) What is the lining epithelium of uterine tube?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The uterine (fallopian) tube is lined by simple columnar epithelium, consisting mainly of:

  • Ciliated columnar cells → propel the ovum toward the uterus

  • Non-ciliated secretory cells → provide nutrients and support

Therefore, among the given options, ciliated columnar epithelium is the best answer.

Exam pearl:
“Uterine tube → ciliated simple columnar epithelium.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২২) Which one is a derivative of foregut?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The pancreas is a derivative of the foregut, developing from dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds arising from the duodenum.

Embryological derivatives:

  • Foregut → pancreas, stomach, liver, proximal duodenum

  • Midgut → jejunum, appendix, proximal 2/3 of transverse colon

  • Hindgut → sigmoid colon, distal 1/3 of transverse colon, rectum

Exam pearl:
“Pancreas = Foregut derivative.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৩) Which structure is in anterior relation of right kidney?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The second part of the duodenum is an important anterior relation of the right kidney, particularly near the renal hilum.

Other relations:

  • Spleen → anterior relation of left kidney

  • Pancreas → mainly anterior relation of left kidney

  • Diaphragm → posterior relation of the kidneys

Exam pearl:
“Right kidney anterior relation → 2nd part of duodenum.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৪) Oocytes develop from -
Anatomy 05.exp:
Oocytes ultimately develop from primordial germ cells (PGCs). These cells migrate to the developing gonads and differentiate into oogonia, which then develop into primary oocytes.

Developmental sequence:

Primordial germ cell → Oogonia → Primary oocyte → Secondary oocyte → Ovum

  • Primordial germ cells → give rise to oocytes

  • Coelomic epithelium → contributes to ovarian follicular cells

  • Mesenchyme → contributes to ovarian stromal tissue

  • Paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct → forms uterine tubes, uterus, and upper vagina

Exam pearl:
“Oocyte origin = Primordial germ cell.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৫) Which one is secreted by delta cell of pancreas?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The delta (δ) cells of the pancreatic islets (Islets of Langerhans) secrete somatostatin.

  • Delta (δ) cells → Somatostatin

  • Alpha (α) cells → Glucagon

  • Beta (β) cells → Insulin

  • PP/F cells → Pancreatic polypeptide

Exam pearl:
“Delta cell → Somatostatin.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৬) Constricted part of the uterus is known as-
Anatomy 05.exp:
The isthmus of the uterus is the narrow/constricted portion between the body of the uterus and the cervix.

  • Fundus → rounded upper part

  • Body → main central portion

  • Isthmus → narrow constricted part

  • Cervix → lower neck-like part of uterus

Exam pearl:
“Constricted part of uterus = Isthmus.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৭) Which one is the ventral branch of abdominal aorta?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The coeliac trunk is an unpaired ventral (anterior) branch of the abdominal aorta. It supplies the derivatives of the foregut.

Major branches of the coeliac trunk:

  • Left gastric artery

  • Splenic artery

  • Common hepatic artery

Other options:

  • Inferior phrenic → paired lateral branch

  • Middle suprarenal → paired lateral branch

  • Common iliac → terminal branch of abdominal aorta

Exam pearl:
“Unpaired ventral branches of abdominal aorta → Coeliac trunk, SMA, IMA.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৮) Which one is primary support of uterus?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The cardinal (transverse cervical) ligaments, along with the uterosacral ligaments and pelvic floor, provide the major support to the uterus.

Among the given options:

  • Broad ligament → mainly a peritoneal fold; not the primary support

  • Uterovesical fold → peritoneal fold

  • Rectovaginal fold → peritoneal fold

  • Round ligament → helps maintain anteversion of the uterus but is not the primary support

Exam pearl:
“Primary uterine support = Cardinal (transverse cervical) ligament.”

Anatomy 05.question: ২৯) Which one is not the content of portal triad??
Anatomy 05.exp:
The portal triad consists of three structures within the portal tract:

  • Portal vein → brings nutrient-rich blood from the GI tract

  • Hepatic artery → supplies oxygenated blood

  • Bile duct(ule) → carries bile away from the liver

Hepatic vein is not part of the portal triad; it drains blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava.

Exam pearl:
“Portal triad = Portal vein + Hepatic artery + Bile duct.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩০) Which one is the Normal position of uterus?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The normal position of the uterus is anteverted and anteflexed.

  • Anteversion → uterus is tilted forward relative to the vagina.

  • Anteflexion → body of uterus is bent forward relative to the cervix.

  • Retroversion/retroflexion → backward positioning, which is not the usual normal position.

Since the question asks for the normal position and only one option is expected, anteversion is the best answer.

Exam pearl:
“Normal uterus = Anteverted + Anteflexed.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩১) Which one is true ligament of liver?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Ligamentum venosum is a true ligament of the liver because it is a fibrous remnant of the fetal ductus venosus.

The other options are peritoneal ligaments:

  • Falciform ligament → peritoneal fold

  • Coronary ligament → peritoneal reflection

  • Right triangular ligament → peritoneal fold

Exam pearl:
True ligaments of liver = Ligamentum teres + Ligamentum venosum.

Anatomy 05.question: ৩২) Which one is not content of broad ligament?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The broad ligament of the uterus is a double layer of peritoneum that contains or encloses several structures, including:

  • Uterine tube

  • Round ligament of uterus

  • Ovarian vessels (within the suspensory ligament of ovary, which is related to the broad ligament)

The pubocervical ligament is a fibrous endopelvic fascial ligament that supports the cervix and upper vagina; it is not a content of the broad ligament.

Exam pearl:
“Broad ligament contents → uterine tube + round ligament + ovarian vessels; pubocervical ligament is not a content.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৩) Which one is the common site of gastric ulcer??
Anatomy 05.exp:
The lesser curvature of the stomach, especially near the incisura angularis, is the commonest site of gastric ulcer.

  • Lesser curvature → commonest site

  • Greater curvature → less common

  • Fundus → uncommon

  • Cardiac notch → not a typical site

Exam pearl:
“Gastric ulcer → lesser curvature, especially near incisura angularis.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৪) Male homologous of vagina is-
Anatomy 05.exp:
The prostatic utricle is considered the male homologous structure of the vagina and uterus. It is an embryological remnant of the Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts.

  • Prostatic utricle → male homologous of vagina/uterus

  • Testes → homologous to ovaries

  • Scrotum → homologous to labia majora

  • Penis → homologous to clitoris

Exam pearl:
“Prostatic utricle = male remnant of Müllerian ducts.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৫) Which is not cardinal feature of large intestine?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The three classic distinguishing features of the large intestine are:

  • Taeniae coli → three longitudinal bands of muscle

  • Sacculations (haustra) → pouch-like sacculations

  • Appendices epiploicae → fatty peritoneal tags

Peyer's patches are aggregates of lymphoid tissue that are characteristic of the ileum (small intestine), not the large intestine.

Exam pearl:
“Large intestine → Taeniae coli + Haustra + Appendices epiploicae.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৬) Urogenital diaphragm consists of which muscle?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The urogenital diaphragm (in traditional anatomical terminology) contains the external urethral sphincter (sphincter urethrae).

  • Sphincter urethrae → part of the deep perineal pouch/urogenital diaphragm

  • Levator ani → pelvic diaphragm

  • Coccygeus → pelvic diaphragm

  • Dartos → superficial scrotal muscle

Exam pearl:
“Urogenital diaphragm → external urethral sphincter.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৭) Which one is the length of duodenum??
Anatomy 05.exp:
The duodenum is approximately 25 cm (10 inches) long in an adult.

It is divided into 4 parts:

  1. Superior (1st) part

  2. Descending (2nd) part

  3. Horizontal/inferior (3rd) part

  4. Ascending (4th) part

Exam pearl:
“Duodenum ≈ 25 cm (10 inches).”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৮) Which one is the shape of male pelvic inlet?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The male pelvic inlet is typically android in shape, which is more heart-shaped compared with the female pelvis.

  • Male pelvis → Android

  • Female pelvis → Gynaecoid (typically round/oval)

  • Anthropoid → elongated anteroposteriorly

  • Platypelloid → flattened transversely

Exam pearl:
“Male pelvic inlet = Android; Female pelvic inlet = Gynaecoid.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৩৯) What is the most dilated part of GIT?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The stomach is the most dilated part of the gastrointestinal tract (GIT). It acts as a reservoir for food and allows mixing with gastric secretions.

Exam pearl:
“Most dilated part of GIT = Stomach.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪০) Brunner’s glands are present in which part of GIT?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Brunner’s glands are submucosal glands found characteristically in the duodenum. They secrete an alkaline, bicarbonate-rich mucus that helps protect the duodenal mucosa from gastric acid.

  • Brunner’s glands → Duodenum

  • Crypts of Lieberkühn → throughout small intestine and large intestine

  • Peyer’s patches → mainly ileum

Exam pearl:
“Brunner’s glands = Duodenum.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪১) What is the location of rugae in stomach?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Gastric rugae are folds of the mucosa along with the underlying submucosa of the stomach. They allow the stomach to expand when it fills.

Among the given options, mucosa is the best answer.

Exam pearl:
“Gastric rugae → mucosal folds (with submucosa).”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪২) What type of muscle is present in middle one third of esophagus?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The esophagus has different types of muscle along its length:

  • Upper 1/3 → Skeletal muscle

  • Middle 1/3 → Skeletal + smooth muscle

  • Lower 1/3 → Smooth muscle

Therefore, the middle one-third contains both skeletal and smooth muscle.

Exam pearl:
“Esophagus: Upper = skeletal → Middle = mixed → Lower = smooth.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৩) Meissner's plexus is present in which layer of GIT?
Anatomy 05.exp:
Meissner’s plexus (submucosal plexus) is located in the submucosa of the gastrointestinal tract.

It mainly regulates:

  • Glandular secretion

  • Mucosal blood flow

  • Muscularis mucosae activity

In comparison:

  • Meissner’s plexus → Submucosa

  • Auerbach’s (myenteric) plexus → Between circular and longitudinal muscle layers of muscularis externa

Exam pearl:
“Meissner = Submucosal; Auerbach = Myenteric.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৪) Which is not a part of digestive tract?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The digestive tract (alimentary canal) is a continuous tube extending from the mouth to the anus.

It includes:

  • Oral cavity

  • Pharynx

  • Esophagus

  • Stomach

  • Small intestine

  • Large intestine

  • Rectum and anal canal

The liver is an accessory digestive organ, not part of the digestive tract itself.

Exam pearl:
“Digestive tract = mouth → anus; Liver = accessory digestive organ.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৫) White pulp & red pulp are found in.... ?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The spleen has two main histological components:

  • White pulp → lymphoid tissue involved in immune responses

  • Red pulp → removes aged/damaged RBCs and filters blood

Exam pearl:
“White pulp + Red pulp = Spleen.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৬) Which is not a retroperitoneal organ?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The stomach is an intraperitoneal organ, not retroperitoneal.

Retroperitoneal structures include:

  • Kidneys

  • Pancreas (except its tail)

  • Aorta

  • Duodenum (2nd–4th parts)

Exam pearl:
“Stomach = intraperitoneal; Kidney + pancreas + aorta = retroperitoneal.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৭) Portal vein is formed at the level of which vertebra?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The portal vein is formed by the union of the splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein, usually behind the neck of the pancreas at the level of L2 vertebra.

  • Splenic vein + SMV → Portal vein

  • Site → behind neck of pancreas

  • Vertebral level → L2

Exam pearl:
“Portal vein formation → L2, behind neck of pancreas.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৮) What is the content of Calot's triangle?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The cystic artery is the important vascular structure found within Calot’s (hepatobiliary) triangle and is usually the structure sought during cholecystectomy.

Boundaries of Calot’s triangle (modern definition):

  • Cystic duct

  • Common hepatic duct

  • Inferior surface of the liver

Content:

  • Cystic artery

  • Cystic lymph node (node of Lund)

  • Sometimes small lymphatics and connective tissue

Exam pearl:
“Calot’s triangle → Cystic artery.”

Anatomy 05.question: ৪৯) Liver gets maximum blood supply from which vessel?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The liver receives blood from two major sources:

  • Portal vein → ~75% of hepatic blood flow

  • Hepatic artery → ~25% of hepatic blood flow

Although the portal vein supplies most of the blood flow, the hepatic artery provides a greater proportion of the liver's oxygenated blood.

Exam pearl:
“Maximum hepatic blood flow → Portal vein (~75%).”

Anatomy 05.question: ৫০) Which one is called policeman of abdomen?
Anatomy 05.exp:
The greater omentum is known as the “policeman of the abdomen” because it can migrate toward areas of inflammation or infection, helping to wall off and localize intra-abdominal infection.

Exam pearl:
“Policeman of abdomen = Greater omentum.”
